statement: Madinah's population: Emigrants, Aws and Khazraj (recently at war), Arabs who had not accepted Islam, and Jewish tribes with their own forts and law.
Usamah ibn Zayd: before Badr the Prophet passed a gathering containing Muslims, idol-worshippers and Jews.
He had a document written regulating relations among the groups of Madinah; its full text is transmitted by the historians without a complete chain.
notes: Text from Ibn Ishaq (in Ibn Hisham) without isnad; scholars differ on whether it is one document or several, and on its date. Narrated explicitly as the historians' report.

statement: Reported terms: believers are one community; each clan responsible for its blood-money and captives; believers stand together against a wrongdoer even if he is one of their sons.
Reported terms with the Jewish tribes: each has its religion and bears its expenses; mutual help against attackers; sincere counsel and no treachery.
Reported terms: Madinah is a sanctuary for the parties; disputes are referred to Allah and Muhammad.
Anas: the Prophet made the alliance between Quraysh and the Ansar in my house.
Ali's sheet from the Prophet: Madinah is a sanctuary; the protection of Muslims is one, the least of them may extend it; whoever betrays a Muslim in it is cursed by Allah, the angels and all people.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked for the sanctuary and protection clauses; 'the least of them may give it' (yas'a biha adnahum) is in parallel narrations (Bukhari 6755), from memory.

statement: Abdullah ibn Ubayy covered his nose and said 'do not raise dust over us'; told the Prophet not to trouble them in their gatherings; Sa'd ibn Ubadah asked the Prophet to pardon him, explaining that the town had agreed to crown him; the Prophet pardoned him.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked for the opening; the rest from memory of the same narration. Reviewer to check wording.

statement: In Makkah the believers were commanded to restrain themselves; fighting was not permitted until after the Hijrah.
notes: Qur'an 4:77 recalls those told 'restrain your hands'.
Paraphrase of meaning. Reported from Ibn Abbas as the first verse permitting fighting (Tirmidhi 3171, from memory).
